records.summary: The lesson treated a high eval pass rate as evidence the set should be expanded without separating capability evaluation from regression testing; recommended fixed thresholds and schedules without a domain basis; left task and intervention denominators unclear; described online failures as directly reusable eval cases; and printed hard-coded metrics as if derived from observations. records.correction: Distinguish capability-eval saturation from regression-suite purpose; frame the 95% figure, sample cadence and work estimates as constructed examples only. Define task completion, unexpected takeover, token/task and replay-coverage denominators. Treat production events as candidates that require privacy handling, deduplication, expected behavior/rubric review and split governance; preserve trace/version/retirement history and maintain holdout separately. Replace hard-coded values with calculations from labeled synthetic fixtures and report approval and exceptional handoff separately. Qualify causal and agent-vs-traditional-software statements.

records.summary: The lesson used a non-exhaustive four-part framework taxonomy as though it were a broad maturity ranking, described observability as the only production diagnostic, and made unqualified claims about framework capabilities and fixed evaluation times. Execute the lesson fence and require byte-for-byte output agreement.

records.summary: The lesson treated linear chain composition as if all framework chains were linear and compile-time checked, implied graphs automatically supplied serializable checkpoint boundaries, and presented a fixed-iteration scripted loop as model-controlled autonomy. Pin and execute the local comparison fixture and require exact stdout agreement.

records.summary: The lesson conflated LangChain @tool docstrings with machine-checkable field constraints and incorrectly generalized enum behavior; treated unreproducible 0/3 vs 3/3 model results as causal; ranked leak types by unsupported frequency; treated unknown outcomes as categorically non-retriable while implying SDK retries were universal; and used unsupported zero-leak and escape-test generalizations.

records.summary: The lesson overgeneralized that agent state is outside application control, used unreproduced planning and latency summaries to justify unpredictable task duration, and stated provider-agnostic cache/timeout behavior. records.summary: The lesson applied an unintended √2 adjustment to its stated single-group Wald interval-width target, doubling the reported planning sample sizes and then presenting them in gray-rollout guidance. It also treated one severe observation as enough to assess incidence, used fixed rollout percentages, and overclaimed release/model provenance: tool schema hashes did not freeze implementations, first_seen/last_pass fields could not derive current regression status, and a model ID was framed as either silently mutable or fully controllable.
records.correction: Use n≈4 z²p(1-p)/w² only as a single-group normal-approximation planning reference (85/531/2,122/8,486 for p=0.02, z=1.6449, widths 5/2/1/0.5 percentage points); direct real-data reporting to suitable intervals and version comparisons to predeclared two-group/paired designs. Treat severe events as stop-rule signals, not incidence or causal estimates, and remove universal traffic percentages. Expand the release manifest to behavior inputs and per-request model metadata; derive regression status from versioned case results and evaluator provenance. Scope model IDs, aliases, and retirement to provider/API contracts. The Python 3.10.9 offline verifier passes eight checks and matches the full published stdout; provider/network calls are zero.

records.summary: The incident-response lesson generalized provider-specific finish/status, token and cache fields; presented synthetic thresholds and alert priorities as universal; made causal claims from cache/error signals; and included a degradation drill that did not inject a failure. records.summary: The lesson did not make two evidence boundaries explicit: the SQLite claim/dispatch fixture does not implement stale-owner fencing, and the PostgreSQL script takes sequential logical dumps of two separate databases without concurrent writes, so it cannot demonstrate a coordinated cross-service snapshot. The pg_verifybackup section also omitted the WAL tool-version and format limits.
records.correction: State that lease expiry, execution epochs, and stale-worker fencing require separate implementation-specific tests; clarify that the synthetic sequential database dumps do not prove a common point-in-time snapshot; and document that pg_verifybackup WAL checks are version-specific and currently supported only for plain-format backups, with --no-parse-wal for tar format. Keep actual restore/data validation as a separate requirement.
limitations: SQLite and PostgreSQL examples are synthetic local fixtures, not proof of production recovery guarantees.
No provider call, real worker takeover, coordinated cross-service backup, WAL/PITR, or production recovery was tested.

records.summary: The approval lesson referred readers to an earlier trace design that advised retaining raw parameters and return values; newer trace guidance requires field minimization and filtering. The proposal hash could also be read as an integrity control without explaining that an attacker who can change both content and digest can recompute it.
records.correction: Align trace guidance with validated/redacted structured fields and safe summaries or controlled references, linking to the dedicated trace lesson. Clarify that a plain SHA-256 digest supports comparison under stable canonicalization but is not tamper protection unless the proposal record is independently protected; add a source-bound OpenTelemetry GenAI checkpoint for opt-in content attributes and its Development status.
limitations: Synthetic policy simulation only; no real user behavior or approval quality measured.
No production storage integrity, authorization system, logging pipeline, or external side effect tested.

records.summary: The recovery fixture reconciled a lost receipt only when the local state had already become unknown. It missed the crash window where the receiver committed the effect but the caller crashed before persisting the receipt, leaving local approval status as approved; the subsequent expiry check could incorrectly return expired despite an existing receiver result.
records.correction: Check the receiver’s authoritative idempotency ledger for the stable action key and payload fingerprint before expiry handling. Reconcile a matching existing result and persist local success without resending, regardless of stale local approved/unknown state. State explicitly that lookup absence cannot prove no effect unless the receiver contract makes the lookup authoritative; keep expiry as a gate on starting a new effect.
limitations: The deterministic in-memory fixture models an authoritative receiver ledger but does not test a real crash, concurrent worker, persistent store, or production receiver contract.
No production authorization, identity, queue, or external side effect was exercised.

records.summary: The local P5 live-smoke narrative conflated a report snapshot still waiting_approval with its separate terminal snapshot, which records task=failed while the approval and send_notice action are cancelled. It also asserted the sink received no request without a delivery receipt or independent sink receive log.
records.correction: Distinguish the report snapshot from the terminal state and preserve the recorded statuses: waiting_approval snapshot; terminal task failed; approval and send_notice action cancelled; acceptance registry incomplete; live_model_normal evidence unverified; final output not_completed. State that no successful tool result or receipt is present, but do not claim sink non-receipt without an independent receive log.
limitations: The raw run artifacts are local, gitignored and unsigned; a recorded hash does not authenticate them.
No independent sink receive log was present; no provider request or external effect was executed during review.

records.summary: The dated clean-run section inferred that all handoff cost came from finding the script path because the script itself ran in 0.03 seconds. The timing measured only that process, not the path discovery, environment setup, or total handoff.
records.correction: Keep the observed first-command failure (working directory omitted) and the historical script runtime as separate observations. State explicitly that path-discovery time was not separately measured and do not attribute all handoff cost to locating the script; preserve the existing caveat that 0.03 seconds is not complete handoff cost.
limitations: The 0.03-second timing remains a historical observation; its raw timing trace and original environment were not independently replayed.
No clean-checkout or independent human handoff was performed.

records.summary: The retrospective restated an unsupported 2.37x multi-agent cost ratio as a retained same-configuration record and used it to discuss run-to-run variation, contradicting the current data ledger.
records.correction: Keep only the 1.91x and 1.99x ratios listed in the historical summary; say run-level requests and responses are missing and the ratios cannot be independently recalculated or generalized. Explicitly state that the 2.37x claim has no registered original data and was withdrawn.
limitations: No historical provider artifacts were recovered or rerun.
This correction validates consistency with the current internal data ledger, not the original provider measurements.

records.summary: The scope table said “at most one bounded online smoke,” which could be read as a global cap on live invocations even though the P5 runbook advances one wake-up per invocation and allows a fresh synthetic task with a new idempotency key.
records.correction: Describe one predeclared fixed smoke case, bound each task by the configured model-round and per-response output-token limits, and state that each report applies only to its observed task run. Do not imply a global one-invocation quota.
limitations: No provider request or external sink action was performed.
This clarification does not define a production/global smoke invocation quota.

records.summary: The lesson called the chapter 18 30-round/one-round input-token ratio of about 405x a historical observation and billing metric, but the source chapter and DATA.md define it as scenario arithmetic over context and tool-schema tokens.
records.correction: State the numerator and denominator, label the ratio as a fixed-assumption scenario result rather than provider measurement or billing multiplier, and distinguish it from the separate scenario cost units that apply an output weight.
limitations: This verifies arithmetic and evidence classification against the current local chapter and data ledger only.
No historical provider call, usage record, or bill was reproduced.

records.summary: The setup said the endpoint probe reads only three environment variables and listed ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, while the appendix also reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY as its preferred credential variable.
records.correction: Describe three configuration values with two accepted API-key environment-variable names, and list both names plus the code's precedence.
limitations: This checks consistency between the local setup instructions and the probe source; it does not test live credential handling.

records.summary: The probe sends one fixed-order pair of requests, but the surrounding verification instructions could be read as a controlled comparison of tool-definition usage despite cache and backend state changing between calls.
records.correction: Label the pair as a descriptive endpoint probe, and require repeated matched pairs with alternating order and complete cache usage records before estimating a tool-definition effect; if cache state cannot be controlled, report the result descriptively or by cache stratum.
limitations: The measurement-design guidance is an engineering recommendation, not a claim that repeated sampling removes all endpoint confounding.
No provider calls or historical measurements were reproduced.

records.summary: The raw-text comparison intentionally failed without showing output; the scorer example contained contradictory sample provenance comments; incomplete test, provider-error, and Anthropic-handler code excerpts were not labeled as non-runnable.
records.correction: Show the raw string comparison as an executed False result; remove the false production-log description; label incomplete illustrative snippets as unrun; retain the scorer as a synthetic local fixture and verify its exact output.
limitations: This verifies local documentation, sample code and arithmetic only.
It does not reproduce historical provider results or evaluate current models on production tasks.

records.summary: The runnable first-loop example followed API redirects with urllib's default opener, allowing the x-api-key request header to reach a redirect target. It also dispatched a final-round tool proposal with no remaining model request to consume the result, accepted missing/duplicate tool-use IDs, and labeled empty end_turn text completed.
records.correction: Reject HTTP redirects in the API opener; validate all tool-use IDs as non-empty and unique before dispatch; skip tool execution when no model round remains; and return completed_without_text for blank end_turn output. Explain each boundary in the lesson and add offline host-control-flow and loopback credential-forwarding regression checks.
limitations: The verifier uses scripted model responses and a loopback HTTP redirect with a dummy credential; it makes no provider calls or external network requests.
This does not verify production authorization, real endpoint compatibility, model quality, or business task success.

records.summary: The tokenizer migration paragraph generalized the ~30% count change to all Claude 4.7+ models and Mythos Preview, beyond the tokenizer-specific model list in the current official docs. The token-counting example also implied all real multimodal inputs could be counted, while server tools, MCP, and URL/file image/document sources are rejected by the endpoint.
records.correction: Name only Claude Fable 5.1, Mythos 5.1, Fable 5 and Mythos 5 for the documented shared tokenizer statement; disclose count_tokens input limitations and use actual Messages usage for unsupported request shapes.
limitations: The official page was checked on 2026-10-22 and may change.
No live provider request or historical DeepSeek measurement was reproduced.
Offline checks validate selected lesson statements and Python syntax, not provider behavior or every factual claim.

records.summary: The meta checkpoint described max_tokens as guaranteeing an incomplete structure and a JSON parse error whenever the output limit is reached. That overstates the protocol: max_tokens signals that generation reached its ceiling and output may be incomplete, but the stop reason alone does not establish whether a particular JSON string parses or satisfies the task.
records.correction: Reframe the checkpoint conditionally: inspect stop_reason, parse and validate the actual output, and recover only when the result is incomplete or invalid.
limitations: The correction is grounded in the documented stop-reason semantics and a local content check; no provider response was generated.
Whether any particular truncated response remains parseable is input/output specific and must be tested on the actual response.

records.summary: The prior review artifact recorded 7 passing checks while its executable verifier currently runs 8; the tracker also said 6/6. The stored evidence count therefore understated the verification actually performed.
records.correction: Re-run the issue verifier, update its result to 8/8, and align the tracker with the executable test count. Keep this correction separate from W6 full-lesson coverage and do not imply the unavailable historical provider experiment was reproduced.
limitations: This corrects verification bookkeeping only; it does not change the lesson's historical evidence limits.
The 8 checks are offline content/code invariants, not provider behavior or task-quality evidence.

records.summary: The SQLite example's prose said the host first persisted a stable action_id, but the code only accepted it as an input and did not demonstrate that host persistence. The code also treated tenant/action/account identifiers as valid when they were whitespace-only or non-string; the tenant input could be mistaken for authenticated identity.
records.correction: Scope the SQLite code to receiver-side atomic local effects/results and state that a trusted host must persist and reuse the action ID before invoking a retryable effect. Reject non-string and blank identifiers before database activity. Explicitly state that the example does not authenticate or authorize, and require authorization before both returning a cached result and executing a new effect.
limitations: The local SQLite fixture verifies only same-database behavior and input validation; production identity, authorization, persistence and cross-system effects remain untested.
Historical DeepSeek tool/error/retry observations remain unreproduced because raw requests, responses and scorer are unavailable.

records.summary: The published `unknown` example contradicted its own schema: it included a forbidden `confirmation: null` property and placed a prose explanation in `evidence` despite instructing readers to use resolvable event IDs. The provider-facing schema also used `minLength`, which current Claude Structured Outputs documentation lists as unsupported. The progress helper accepted booleans because Python treats bool as int, and did not validate input types.
records.correction: Make the unknown example conform to its schema and use a synthetic event ID. Remove `minLength` from the provider-facing schema, explain the provider limitation, and require host-side semantic checks for non-empty strings. Validate integer counts without accepting bool, validate dynamic status values, and exercise invalid cases locally.
limitations: Ajv tests establish local JSON Schema behavior only, not provider schema acceptance or generated model outputs.
Synthetic progress helper fixtures do not replace user research or screen reader testing.

records.summary: The W6 progress counter incremented two lesson IDs that were already present in its explicit 59-ID master list when they were re-reviewed, producing overstated 65/144 and 66/144 snapshots. The master list also omitted several later passes.
records.correction: Deduplicate W6 coverage by lesson ID, keep re-review evidence without incrementing the unique count, and restore the missing IDs to the master list. The reconciled current count is 65/144 (45.14%), 79 remain.
limitations: The verifier enforces the reconciled master list and matching current declarations; it does not independently establish the quality of each lesson review.

records.issue: The policy demo defaulted a missing amount to zero for an amount-sensitive action and did not fail closed for malformed trusted policy metadata.
records.correction: Require amount fields where applicable, validate trusted policy inputs and reject malformed values; retain explicit limitations that this teaching function is not a complete authorization boundary.
limitations: No production authorization, complete parameter schema, execution-time revalidation, concurrency behavior, provider output, or external side effects were tested.

records.issue: The lesson called dropping partial output an error and said it should always be retained, contradicting its own task/privacy-dependent policy. It also described JSON as invalid during streaming and labeled the first two failure modes non-errors while saying the third causes billing impact, although the first row was the cancellation/billing case. The fake-tool example did not execute its already-dispatched side-effect branch.
records.correction: Make partial-output retention policy-dependent and require clear user communication; describe intermediate JSON deltas as incomplete rather than invalid; correct the failure-mode framing; extend the local fixture to prove a dispatched side effect may complete after cancellation.
limitations: No provider cancellation, billing, real side effects, production replay, or UX study was performed.

records.issue: The lesson said a criterion needs at least four checklist items while listing five, then concluded that defining “good” means translating it into something automatically decidable, contradicting the preceding human/rubric/judge boundaries.
records.correction: State that the checklist contains five items; clarify that only suitable criteria should be automated and semantic/subjective objectives may use explicit rubrics, human references, or calibrated judges with visible error and scope.
limitations: No judge calibration, human inter-rater study, live model or production task outcome was tested.
